The s, c, tall looped h, accented e and m are separately recoverable. The last place contains dense overlapping blue loops with a rounded bowl and a rightward terminal, favoring a. notes: Handwritten letter page on squared paper, attributed to P. Deligne by the supplied H description, dated Bures sur Yvette, le 21 octobre 1968 and addressed Cher Grothendieck. The underlined proposition claims that a compact complex analytic space X is a scheme exactly when its reduction is. The writer reduces to a square-zero ideal, introduces analytic and algebraic infinitesimal extension groups and a locally given cotangent complex, then displays the sheaf Hom and Ext and a two-row comparison diagram. The final paragraph claims exactness and outer vertical isomorphisms by GAGA, leaving an inclusion of images to show. These are page claims, not independently verified conclusions. The word supposer and the phrase comparer les images de alpha et beta are cancelled and retained as deletions. There is no document title beyond the underlined word proposition. No manuscript page number or total-page count is visible; the lower-left 74 is recorded only as an archive comment. H’s description calls this the first of two sheets, but that count is not added to the transcription. The upper-left pencil note has an explicit question mark after the SGA 7 VI reference. Its opening word/case, the introductory K, the crowded final letter of schéma, the display label, and the two detached-mark loci retain editorial uncertainty. H is descriptive only: all h_reading values are null and all diff_h values false.
math_reading_decisions: The proposition has X_{\mathrm{red}} with a lowered joined red and no visible acute; the later X_0 indices are small lowered ovals. No normalization to réd was made.
The pencil groups are VI and II, each with a distinct upper and lower rule; the question mark follows the VI reference.
The ideal letter has the repeated looped script form \mathscr{N}, distinct from the plain crossed Xs.
The two extension-group letters are upright ordinary E; an and alg are raised words. Singular Soit is retained before the pair.
The introduction retains \unsure{K|\mathbb{K}} because the thick left side can be a retrace or a separate doubled stroke; the K occurrences in formulas have ordinary single stems.
The Hom initial has crossing loops and the Ext initial has curved upper and lower parts, represented by \mathscr{H}om and \mathscr{E}xt. The Ext degree is the visible raised upright 1.
The cohomology degrees and qualifiers keep the visible stepped rise: H^{1^{\mathrm{alg}}}, H^{1^{\mathrm{an}}}, H^0, H^{0^{\mathrm{an}}}. No alg is supplied to the upper-right H^0.

The implication has two shafts and a right head. The comparison diagram has six rightward arrows and three downward arrows; the two rightmost horizontal arrows carry alpha above and beta below, respectively.
The final image relation is \operatorname{Im}(\beta)\subset\operatorname{Im}(\alpha), with an open left-curved inclusion sign and no lower equality bar.
The low dotted i and looped l settle il s\textquotesingle obtient as lower case after the full stop. This textual target was inspected, not mathematically inferred.
The first display label retains a new 1/i ambiguity owing to the displaced upper point; its later (1) reference is independently legible and retained.
No proof, external background verification, or mathematical computation was performed; notation consistency was used only as a diagnostic before returning to the visible strokes.
